stance.label: Cycle bull · day 4 below the 200-day average

headline: Day 4 below the 200-day average, so the Nov 16 close triggers the hedge; short-term holders are on a 6th straight day of concentrated loss-taking.
summary: The plan's hedge is one day away: a Nov 16 close below 72,923 cuts 20%, and getting back above needs an 11.6% rally. Short- and long-term holders are both selling at a loss, and the Dawn Index heat fell to 6.7, into Deep night. Next, watch 62K: from there down to 58K there are only 130K more short-term holder coins, so a break has no thick cost layer under it.

overview.lead: A 1.9% bounce didn't change the structure: short-term holders are in their 6th day of concentrated loss-taking, long-term holders are selling at a loss too, and the hedge fires tomorrow.
points: Close 65,315 with an intraday low of 61,970, finishing at 81% of the day's range; volume was 1.4x the 20-day average.
Short-term holders realized 8,969 BTC of losses against 2,196 BTC of profit, four times as much loss (CheckOnChain, Nov 15).
Fear & Greed is 10, 6th percentile of the past year; Polymarket puts a December hike at 96%.

cycle.lead: The Dawn Index heat dropped to 6.7, into Deep night, while the weekly trend score deepened to −0.83: bottom-zone valuation with a falling trend.
points: The market stage is still bull, day 38, with the 200-day average at 72,923 still rising; only 1 of 6 supporting lights is on (exchange supply).

Yesterday's note gave the Dawn Index heat as 33.4; correction: that was the reading 4 weeks ago. It was 11.8 on Nov 13 and 6.7 on Nov 14, and below 10 is Deep night (bottom zone). In the 62 past weeks spent in Deep night, price was higher a year later 98% of the time, median +83%; that is valuation history, and the trend half still points down.
Weekly trend score −0.43 → −0.83, week 2 on the negative side; it takes 4 weeks to flip to bear.
Day 405 after this cycle's top, down 47.7%; the three prior cycles were all below −75% on the same day.

market.lead: Day 2 of the bottom combination: Sell Pressure Index at 100, momentum quality 0.12.
points: Since 2012 the combination has appeared 20 times; 90 days later price was higher in 12, median +17.8%. The median drawdown before it ended was still −12.2%, and all 6 cases since 2023 ended in a gain.
This leg is down 24.6% over 55 days since Sep 21, and 12.9% below its end line at 73,732.

deriv.lead: Leverage got its funding reset but not its positions: weighted funding fell from 4.3% to 1.0%, while 75.5% of accounts are still long.
points: Binance −0.27%, Bybit −1.36%, OKX −1.43%, with only Hyperliquid at +11%; open interest is 326K BTC, down 3.8% in 7 days.

7-day implied volatility fell from 58.5% to 46.4%, and its gap over 90-day shrank from 16 to 6 points, so most of yesterday's panic pricing is gone; implied also dropped below realized, which leaves options relatively cheap.

Estimated long liquidation bands sit at 61.4–61.9K (5.6% below the close) and 59.5–60.3K, based on Coinalyze aggregated open interest plus assumed leverage; trading into them would set off a batch of market sells.
The biggest book walls are a 237M ask at 65,000 and a 227M bid at 64,000, both on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: The US side is still distributing and the buyers are in Asia: Coinbase's 30-day taker selling is the heaviest since 2021, and the Korea premium is at its high for the year.
points: This page's finding: Coinbase spot shows 17K BTC of net taker selling over 30 days, 0th percentile since 2021; the Korea premium is 2.99%, above this year's prior high of 2.5% on Feb 4.
ETFs −$185M on Nov 13, a 7th straight outflow day, −$2.08B over 20 days (CoinMarketCap); no new data over the weekend.
Stablecoins at $287.1B, down 1.5% in 7 days (DefiLlama); USDT at 0.9995 has its lowest month-to-date average in 50 months.
The estimated ETF holder cost is above price, with the close 17.3% below it; the deepest was −26.4% on Jun 30.

onchain.lead: Selling has spread from short-term to long-term holders: coins long-term holders sold today were at an average 24% loss.
points: This page's finding: 62–66K is the thickest short-term holder layer, and only 22.8% of their supply is in profit; STH-SOPR at 0.971 has been below 1 for 10 days.
LTH-SOPR at 0.764 is 8.8th percentile of 4 years; long-term holders' 7-day realized loss rose to $2.09B, against $3.6B at the Jun 30 low (Bitview, Nov 15).
Long-term holders in loss: 41.7%; on the estimate, a drop to 61,000 would push it past this cycle's high of 45.4% (CheckOnChain).
7-day hashrate 894 EH/s, −11.8% on the week; the next difficulty adjustment on Nov 27 is estimated at +0.3%.

exit.lead: No exit rule has fired; day 4 below the 200-day average, and a Nov 16 close under 72,923 cuts 20% as a hedge.
points: The buy-back condition is close too: 5 closes back above the average, or the MVRV Z 7-day average under 0.5. MVRV Z was 0.33 on the day with a 0.57 7-day average (CoinMetrics, Nov 14), so the hedge and the buy-back could both fire within days.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak is 0.428, far from the 0.75 line at 111,868; the three top gauges read 10 / 9 / 25, all low.

findings.title: Most short-term holders are underwater; below 62K it's up to long-term holders
findings.lean_why: Most short-term holders are already underwater and taking losses, so the coins left to sell are shrinking; but short-term cost is thin below 62K, so price can move fast through it.
findings.what: How much new selling appears at 62K? Not much from short-term holders: the 65,315 close already leaves 77% of their supply underwater (Bitview), and price sits on their thickest layer at 64–66K (539K BTC, CheckOnChain Nov 15).
findings.why: Split by cohort. Short-term holders hold 3.79M BTC at a 74,071 cost; at a 64K close 3.20M would be underwater, and at 58K only 590K more, with just over 60K BTC per 2,000 band between 62K and 58K. For long-term holders, 6.95M would be underwater at 64K and 7.72M at 58K, 770K more, more than short-term holders add. Both sides are selling at a loss: STH-SOPR 0.971 below 1 for 10 days, concentrated loss-taking on day 6, short-term holder losses four times their profits; LTH-SOPR 0.764 and long-term holders' 7-day realized loss up to $2.09B (Bitview). Over 30 days an estimated 1.29M short-term coins moved and 1.63M were newly acquired, mostly at 62–66K.
findings.alt: The current cohort split is CheckOnChain's age-based actual; the 30-day turnover is estimated (2.0% off the actual). Per-UTXO data counts exchange wallet reshuffles as turnover. A single-day LTH-SOPR of 0.76 could be a few large transfers; the 7-day average is 0.956. Paper losses don't mean selling either: long-term holders in loss hit 45.4% on Jun 30, which was the low.
findings.history: Widespread underwater short-term holders taking concentrated losses have usually been near local lows, with no guarantee of a last leg: with price below the 200-day average, such loss-taking occurred 23 times since 2012, and 30 days later price was higher in 10, median −0.8%, about the same as any day. This time long-term holders' realized loss of $2.09B is still below the $3.1–3.6B at this cycle's three lows.
findings.so: What changes is who sells next: most of what short-term holders can sell is already underwater, so selling below 62K would come mainly from long-term holders. What doesn't change is the hedge timing; the Nov 16 close still decides the plan's move.
findings.next: By Nov 20: loss-taking intensity under 2 with price holding above 62K means short-term holders are done and 64–66K turns into support; a close below 62,000 means the layer gave way and selling passes to long-term holders.

findings.title: US spot is selling, Korea is buying at a premium that's at a yearly high
findings.lean_why: US taker selling is the heaviest since 2021, the Asian premium buying is small in size, and past high Korea premiums were usually followed by lower prices 90 days later.
findings.what: The buying of the past two days is in Asia: the Korea premium is 2.99%, above this year's prior high of 2.5% on Feb 4, while Coinbase spot shows 17K BTC of net taker selling over 30 days, 0th percentile since 2021 (Upbit, Coinalyze, Nov 15).
findings.why: Based on flows.kp and deriv.taker.cb; no signal listed. The Korea premium's 7-day average is 2.03%, against under 1% a week ago, and OKX's OTC USDT/CNY rate briefly carried a 1.5% premium on Nov 14. On the US side, Coinbase has 8,631 BTC of net taker selling in 7 days and ETFs have 7 straight outflow days; yet the USDT-adjusted Coinbase premium was near 0 on the day, so the selling is being absorbed at par. Across three spot venues the 30-day total is −14K BTC, lighter than the −24K median since 2021, so the selling is concentrated on Coinbase.
findings.alt: Weekend FX carries Friday's ECB reference rate, so any weekend won move distorts the premium; Coinbase taker selling could also be ETF issuer sales or market makers moving inventory. It's one venue on each side and very different sizes, so a Korean premium doesn't mean large buying.
findings.history: Of 10 high Korea-premium stretches since 2017, price was higher 90 days later in only 4, median −12.2%; today's 2.99% is only the 69th percentile of 4 years, short of a hot stretch.
findings.so: What changes is where the buying is: US spot demand hasn't returned, and the bounce rests on Asia and short covering. What doesn't change is the ETF outflow trend or the cycle view.
findings.next: By Nov 20: a Korea premium still at 2% or more means the Asian buying is lasting; Coinbase's 7-day taker flow turning to net buying means the US selling is over.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Running on Empty
items.points: BTC near 74K, below short-term holder cost of 75.6K, with only about 35% of short-term supply in profit; true market mean 77.5K; two-thirds of short-term supply sits above price, and the only thick layer below is 62–66K. Stablecoins shrank $14.2B in 30 days; the largest long liquidation band is 59.5–62.6K; holding the June low at 58.5K keeps August's trend reversal intact.
items.meaning: Our STH supply in profit is 22.8%; its largest long liquidation band at 59.5–62.6K overlaps our two estimated bands at 59.5–61.9K, and Sunday's low of 61,970 touched the upper edge.

items.title: Bitcoin: Correction or Reset?
items.points: Via media coverage: short-term holder cost 75,717, with BTC below it for 4 days; reclaiming it plus 3 straight ETF inflow days would mark a correction, otherwise a reset; 11 of 14 past breaks were reclaimed within two weeks. Futures open interest 701.9K BTC, up 3.3% while price fell, funding about 11% annualized.
items.meaning: Original not read, so not used as evidence; by its split, a close 12.6% below the short-term holder cost and 7 straight ETF outflow days still put us on the reset side.
